newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan diplomat reports continued gunfire in Lima.
newsitem.headline: Japan diplomat reports continued gunfire in Lima.

text.p: A Japanese diplomat in the Peruvian capital of Lima said he was caught in a guerrilla attack at the residence of the Japanese ambassador to Peru and could not leave because of continuing gunfire, a Japanese Foreign Ministry official said on Wednesday.

"I first heard several bombs exploding in front of the official residence of the ambassador," the ministry official quoted Hiroyuki Kimoto, who holds the rank of minister at the embassy, as saying in a call from his mobile phone.
Japan's public television network NHK said the guerrillas took 800 hostages but the Foreign Ministry could not confirm this report.

"Then I heard the sound of gunfire. I can't raise my head now because the firing is continuing," Kimoto was quoted as saying. He said he was stuck at a guardpost at the gate of the residence because of the gunfire.

Attempts to call Kimoto again failed, the ministry official said. The call came at 11.15 a.m. Japan time (0215 GMT). The official said he could not confirm the whereabouts of Ambassador Morihisa Aoki and his wife Naoko.

A Peruvian minister and eyewitnesses said about 20 gunmen armed with automatic rifles and grenades attacked the Japanese ambassador's residence on Tuesday and held up to 40 people hostage. Police radio in Lima said six small explosions were heard at the beginning of the attack. The attack began during a reception for Emperor Akihito's birthday which is reported to have been attended by ambassadors from several countries.
